H1.statement: Real sentences minimize dependency length vs. random projective linearization, on both metrics.
H1.role: sanity check -- failure indicates a broken pipeline, not a refuted theory
H1.baseline_note: B2_arity_preserving is reported but not scored: it preserves each node's left/right dependent counts, so it often reproduces the real order exactly and cannot detect a DLM effect.

H2.statement: The head-based metric shows a larger real-vs-random effect than the word-based metric.

coprimary_prob_advantage.statistic: P(real shorter) with ties split, head minus word

H3.statement: Word-based dependency length is derivative of head-based dependency length.
H3.predicted_direction: beta(word_DL) indistinguishable from zero once head_DL is in the model, with beta(head_DL) significant and the nested LR test passing FDR
H3.statistic_note: Scored on whether word_DL retains an independent effect, NOT on shrinkage in |beta(word_DL)|. Logistic coefficients are not collapsible, so a between-model beta comparison measures rescaling rather than derivativeness.
H3.collinearity_note: word_DL and head_DL differences correlate 0.95-0.98 within pairs. The LR test and delta_AUC are the interpretable quantities; individual betas are fragile under this VIF.
